claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is an equiatomic refractory high-entropy alloy.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr can be consolidated by sintering and given a silicide coating by pack cementation.
Silicide-coated HfNbTaTiZr will resist long-term erosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum better than conventional dipping-equipment materials.
A temperature around 660°C is typical for liquid-aluminum hot-dip plating exposure.
The silicide layer remains protective during extended contact with liquid aluminum.
The silicide coating can develop self-healing (Zr,Hf)O2 particles inside microcracks.
During exposure, the silicide coating reacts to form a protective oxide scale.
The protective oxide scale limits aluminum diffusion into the refractory alloy.
The protective oxide scale limits chemical attack of the refractory alloy by liquid aluminum.
Self-healing is driven by silicon diffusion and the formation of oxide particles.
The proposed self-healing mechanism improves coating stability against liquid-aluminum corrosion.
Silicide-coated HfNbTaTiZr will have significantly lower erosion and corrosion rates than an uncoated HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
Silicide-coated HfNbTaTiZr will have significantly lower erosion and corrosion rates than carbon steels or stainless steels.
The reduced erosion and corrosion will extend the service life of dipping and plating equipment.
Carbon steels and stainless steels used in dipping equipment are rapidly corroded by high-temperature liquid aluminum.
Performance of the coating may depend on temperature and aluminum-bath chemistry.
Improved oxidation resistance has been documented for silicide-coated HfNbTaTiZr or similar alloys.
The cited study does not establish resistance to direct chemical attack by liquid aluminum.
